mechanism: ISI ProSpread SMA buckets H1 history (e.g. 30–90 days) by clock hour within a chosen session window; for each hour computes Prob(up/down), average body, avg move, and min/max range. Dashboard flags UP/DOWN/NEUTRAL with Prob% so the hour itself is a recurring directional regime.
data_needed: H1 OHLC for symbol or K1*P1−K2*P2 spread; InpStartHour/InpEndHour; InpHistoryDays; formula type 1 or 3 for signed body.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, EURUSD−GBPUSD spread; H1; London-focused windows e.g. 8:00–12:00; also session map covering Sydney/Tokyo/London/NY.
why_new_for_mis: Turns clock-hour seasonality into an explicit per-hour directional-probability regime sensor (not a lagging MA), with expected move size for MIS session gating.
quote: the price at the same hour on different days has a statistically significant tendency to move in a certain direction with predictable force

mechanism: Formula 2 Volatility Index: ISI=(High−Low)/Point for one symbol, or (K1*(H1−L1)−K2*(H2−L2))/Point for a spread. High ISI → elevated hourly vol / breakout-prone; low → consolidation. Sharp jumps flagged as approaching breakout.
data_needed: Per-bar High/Low (and second symbol if spread); symbol Point; optional lot coeffs.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD example ~150 pts/hour; EURUSD/GBPUSD range differential; H1 analysis TF.
why_new_for_mis: Hour-bucketed range-in-points volatility sensor that also works on relative spread ranges—direct MIS vol calendar by clock hour.
quote: High values of the indicator demonstrate high volatility in a given hour, which indicates the likelihood of a breakout and strong moves. Low values, on the contrary, indicate a period of calm and consolidation.

mechanism: Maps FX sessions (Sydney/Wellington calm; Asia low-liq/tight ranges; London high volume ~30% daily; NY aggressive; London–NY overlap 16:00–19:00 hottest) as liquidity/volatility temperament regimes; quiet hours → high spreads / low liquidity.
data_needed: Session open/close clocks (DST-aware); optional I-session style session coloring; symbol universe by center (JPY/AUD Asia; EUR/GBP London; USD/CAD NY).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: AUDNZD, AUDUSD, USDJPY, EURUSD, GBPUSD, USDCAD and majors; intraday session hours.
why_new_for_mis: Codifies geographic session overlaps as liquidity-regime labels MIS can use to gate sensors by expected participation and spread cost.
quote: Overlapping trading sessions during the day: the greatest activity and volatility occur during periods of their intersection (London/New York).

mechanism: Formula 0: Spread=K1*Price1−K2*Price2, then SMA(N). ISI above zero → symbol1 relatively strong vs symbol2; below → weak; zero-line cross = relative-strength regime flip. Compare current spread to hour-window SMA for overbought/oversold of the pair differential.
data_needed: Two correlated symbols’ prices; lot coeffs; SMA period (e.g. 14); optional hour filter.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD/GBPUSD (coeffs 1.0/0.8 example); also XAUUSD/XAGUSD mentioned; H1.
why_new_for_mis: Pair-spread SMA as a market-neutral relative-strength sensor—MIS can track cross-asset leadership without directional FX beta.
quote: A value above zero indicates the potential strength of the first instrument in relation to the second, a value below zero indicates weakness. Crossing the zero line may indicate a change in trend.

mechanism: Competitive Learning Algorithm (CLA_L) is a population metaheuristic (students/classes/teachers) tested on Hilly/Forest/Megacity synthetic functions; no market regime, vol, liquidity, or sequence sensing is built.
why_new_for_mis: No MIS sensing content after full read—optimizer implementation/benchmark only.
quote: In this article, we will examine in detail the principles of CLA, its mathematical basis, implementation features, and compare its effectiveness with other popular metaheuristics on our standard test functions.

mechanism: CoSO Theory: Community of Scientists Optimization (journals, grants, outsiders, hiring) as a PSO-like metaheuristic with adaptive Ω from fitness σ; no market sensing—search-space optimization only. Practice article continues implementation/tests.
why_new_for_mis: Theory half of CoSO series is pure optimizer design—no MIS market sensor.
quote: Unlike classical bio-inspired algorithms, CoSO replicates the unique characteristics of scientific activity: publishing results in journals, competition for grants

mechanism: CoSO Practice finishes AssignFunds/CreateOutsiders/HireResearchers/UpdateOmega(σ) and ranks CoSO at 43.37% on AO bench—still no price/vol/liquidity market sensing.
why_new_for_mis: Practice half confirms CoSO is an AO ranking entry, not a market intelligence sensor.
quote: The CoSO algorithm demonstrates average results on the test functions, achieving 43% of the maximum possible performance.

mechanism: Reporting EA exports deal CSV and launches Python to build PDF/HTML with net profit, max drawdown, Sharpe-like ratio, equity curve—post-trade account reporting, not live market regime/vol/liquidity sensing.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Account trade history (~90 days export); any symbols present in deals.
why_new_for_mis: Full read shows tooling for report delivery/JSON handshake—no new MIS market sensor.
quote: The EA exports a dated CSV of trading history and launches the Python report generator, which processes the CSV to compute analytics, produce charts, and write the final report (PDF)

mechanism: Duelist Algorithm: winners innovate, losers learn, champions train offspring—metaheuristic on synthetic AO functions; trading mentions are metaphor only.
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing after full read.
quote: we will examine the mathematical basis of the Duelist Algorithm in detail, implement it in MQL5, and conduct a comparative analysis with other population-based optimization methods.

mechanism: Dream Optimization Algorithm (DOA): group memory, cosine-modulated forgetting, dream sharing, 99%/1% explore/exploit—AO for parameter search, not a live market sensor.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Synthetic AO functions; trading-parameter tuning mentioned only as use-case.
why_new_for_mis: Optimizer article—no MIS sensing construct on price data.
quote: DOA simulates three key aspects of the sleep process: partial memory retention, selective forgetting with subsequent replenishment of information, and the exchange of "dreams" between agents

mechanism: Bison Algorithm (BIA): 80% swarm vs 20% runners, weighted elite center, run-direction explorers—population AO on synthetic functions only.
why_new_for_mis: No market sensing after full read.
quote: The key features of BIA are two fundamental principles borrowed from the behavior of bison: the ability to move dynamically and a defensive strategy.

mechanism: Dingo Optimization Algorithm: group attack / chase / scavenging / survival metaheuristic; poor AO score (~35%); no market sensing.
quote: DOA models three main hunting strategies of dingoes: Group attack, Chase, Scavenging. Additionally, the algorithm includes a survival mechanism

mechanism: Build daily session high/low over RangeStartTime+RangeDuration; UpperVolStop=SessionHigh+ATR*ATRMultiplier, LowerVolStop=SessionLow−ATR*ATRMultiplier. After session end, ask≥SessionHigh is a high-breakout candidate; only if ask≥UpperVolStop is it a cleared (genuine) vol breakout—else uncleared/false. Symmetric on lows.
data_needed: Intraday ticks/bid-ask; session clock params; iATR(ATRPeriod e.g. 14); ATRMultiplier (default 2.0).
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EA on _Symbol/_Period; backtest shown on H1 ~2-month window; session minutes-from-midnight inputs.
why_new_for_mis: Explicit genuine-vs-false breakout classifier using ATR clearance beyond the session range—MIS can sense vol-confirmed range breaks vs noise pierces.
quote: By requiring price to move beyond both the range boundary and a volatility threshold, the system helps distinguish genuine breakouts from market noise.

mechanism: On first pierce of SessionHigh: if price has NOT cleared UpperVolatilityStop → treat as false breakout and fade (sell); if cleared → trade breakout direction (buy). Mirror on SessionLow. One-shot HighBreakoutTriggered/LowBreakoutTriggered flags per session.
data_needed: SessionHigh/Low; Upper/LowerVolatilityStop; CurrentTick ask/bid; breakout-triggered flags.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: _Symbol session EA; H1 backtest window in article.
why_new_for_mis: Operationalizes uncleared vs cleared breakouts into opposite change signals—MIS regime-change cue gated by vol threshold.
quote: Check if price has cleared volatility stop… Regular breakout - execute buy… False breakout - execute sell (fade)

mechanism: UT Bot: nLoss=a*ATR(c); trail ratchets up in uptrends as max(prev_trail, src−nLoss) and down as min(prev_trail, src+nLoss); resets on direction change. Distance widens in high ATR and tightens in low ATR—volatility-adaptive trend envelope. Optional Heikin Ashi src.
data_needed: iATR(period c default 10); sensitivity a default 1.0; close or HA close series.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GOLD/XAUUSD H1/M15; GBPUSD & GBPJPY M15; any asset/TF claimed; EA also uses D1/H4 EMA filters.
why_new_for_mis: Classic ATR stair-step trail as a live vol-scaled regime boundary MIS can read without multi-MA stacks.
quote: The UT BOT uses average true range (ATR) to dynamically adjust the distance of the trailing stop from the current trading price, making it responsive to the ever-changing market conditions.

mechanism: Buy when src crosses above trail (src>trail_curr && src1<=trail1); sell when trail crosses above src. pos_arr flips +1/−1 on those crosses—hard regime-change events from price vs ATR trail.
data_needed: Current/prior close (or HA); current/prior trail; optional alert de-dup by bar time.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: GOLD H1 demo; GBPUSD/GBPJPY M15 EA tests Jan–Apr 2025; London/NY session gate 08–20 GMT in EA.
why_new_for_mis: Non-repainting crossover of price through an ATR trail gives MIS a crisp long/short regime-flip sensor usable across TFs.
quote: Buy Signal ("UT Long"): Triggered when the current price crosses above the trailing stop… Sell Signal ("UT Short"): Triggered when the current price crosses below the trailing stop

mechanism: GaussianMixture(n_components=6, full covariance, reg_covar=0.1) fit on engineered float features; each bar gets cluster id interpreted as regimes (strong/weak bull, low/high-vol sideways, weak/strong bear). Cluster becomes a contextual feature for downstream models.
data_needed: Feature matrix (indicators + generated combos); sklearn GaussianMixture; drop label cols; median-impute inf/nan.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD; hourly-scale history in augmentation discussion.
why_new_for_mis: Unsupervised 6-state regime label in indicator feature space—MIS can treat GMM cluster as a soft market-state sensor before supervised heads.
quote: In the context of financial markets, this means dividing into regimes - bull market, bear market, sideways movement, high volatility, low volatility.

mechanism: Per symbol: D1 True Range → 14-day ATR; risk_per_lot=(ATR/point)*tick_value; allocate TOTAL_PORTFOLIO_RISK/n_symbols equally; lot = risk_budget/risk_per_lot normalized to volume_step. High-vol names automatically get smaller size—portfolio vol sensor driving exposure.
data_needed: mt5.copy_rates D1 (≥20 bars); symbol_info point/tick_value/volume_min/step; TOTAL_PORTFOLIO_RISK.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD; D1 ATR window 14.
why_new_for_mis: Cross-sectional ATR risk-per-lot as a multi-symbol volatility sensor that directly maps into comparable portfolio weights for MIS.
quote: ATR (Average True Range) becomes the basis of our risk management system. This indicator measures the average volatility of an instrument over 14 days

mechanism: Build RSI/MACD/ATR/Williams%R/Aroon/Efficiency Ratio (+ random algebraic/rolling feature combos), RFECV select ~15 features, train XGBClassifier inside BaggingClassifier with GridSearchCV; online predict >0.5 → buy else sell. Per-symbol thread with time-split train/test.
data_needed: OHLCV history; pandas feature pipeline; XGBoost+sklearn Bagging/RFECV/GMM; MT5 Python API ticks/orders.
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD, GBPUSD, AUDUSD, NZDUSD, USDCAD; FORWARD cutoff datetime(2025,1,1); ~64–65% reported test accuracy.
why_new_for_mis: End-to-end multi-symbol sequence/classifier sensor stack (features→GMM context→XGB ensemble) MIS can treat as a learned directional probability feed.
quote: Python is responsible for the "brains" - data collection, pre-processing, feature creation, model training, and trading signal generation.
